newsitem.title: USA: Dole visits ancestral gravesite in Ohio.
newsitem.headline: Dole visits ancestral gravesite in Ohio.

text.p: Paying a homage to his family's pre-Kansas roots, Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole on Thursday visited the gravesite of his great-great grandfather, Michael Dole, who died in 1867.

As the evening sun hung low in the sky behind him and a group of townspeople looked on, Dole laid a bouquet of flowers at the tall, white tombstone marking the grave. Alongside that marker was the smaller stone of a granddaughter to Michael Dole, Minne Dole, who died at the age of four in 1869.

Dole was accompanied at the small, rural cemetery by Alan Benjamin, a retired AT&T employee who uncovered the Dole family connection while working on a history for Montpelier's 150th anniversary celebration last year.

Later Dole told a crowd at the Williams County fair in this town in northwestern Ohio: "I know we're talking about the future, but it's always good to know where you came from, what kind of people you came from.
"I've been looking for rich relatives all my life. Maybe I'll find one before I leave here," he quipped.
Dole's great-grandfather, James Dole, moved to Bunker Hill, Kansas, near Dole's hometown of Russell, around 1886, according to an article on the family history by the Cleveland Plain Dealer.
Benjamin said the graveside meeting was an emotional one for him, and, asked if Dole appeared emotional also, Benjamin said, "yes, I think so."
"We just discussed his family history. He was interested in the relationships and he saw tombstones here that he recognises the names," Benjamin told reporters.

After the cemetary stop, Dole drove a few miles to visit a currently unoccupied ancestral home, where he met a local family, unrelated to him, which bought it recently, and continued catching up on family history with Benjamin.
Members of the Ohio branch of the family included a relative, also named Robert Dole, who was wounded in the Civil War and was active in area Republican politics.
